name: Gentle Neck & Shoulder Rolls
instructions: Sit or stand tall with relaxed shoulders.
Gently roll your shoulders backward 10 times in a slow circle, then forward 10 times.
Lower your right ear toward your right shoulder for 10 seconds, then repeat on the left.
Breathe smoothly without forcing any stretch.
safetyPrecautions: Do not drop your head backward abruptly or roll forcefully.
easierModification: Perform seated comfortably against a chair back.
benefits: Releases upper body tension from studying or desk work, improving circulation.

name: Hip Circles & Ankle Rotations
nameHi: हिप सर्कल्स और टखने का घुमाव
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, hands on hips.
Make smooth, controlled hula-hoop circles with your hips, 8 times clockwise, 8 times anticlockwise.
Lift one foot slightly and rotate the ankle 10 times each way, then switch legs.
easierModification: Hold onto a sturdy wall or hostel bed for balance.
benefits: Warms up synovial fluid in pelvic joints before movement.

name: Cat-Cow Stretch (Marjaryasana-Bitilasana)
instructions: Start on all fours with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips on a mat or soft rug.
Inhale (Cow): Gently drop your belly toward the mat, lift your chest and gaze slightly upward.
Exhale (Cat): Draw your navel toward your spine and gently round your back, letting your neck relax.
Flow slowly with your natural breath rhythm.
safetyPrecautions: Keep wrists soft; if wrists feel sore, make fists or rest on forearms.
easierModification: Can be done seated in a chair by curving and arching the torso with hands on knees.
benefits: Gently massages pelvic and abdominal organs, relieving cramps and stiffness.

name: Butterfly Pose (Baddha Konasana)
instructions: Sit on the floor with your spine straight. Bend your knees and bring the soles of your feet together.
Hold your feet or ankles with your hands.
Gently flutter your knees up and down like butterfly wings for 30 seconds, then hold steady and breathe deeply.
Keep your shoulders down and relaxed.
safetyPrecautions: Do not force your knees down to the floor. Use cushions under knees if needed.
easierModification: Place a folded blanket or hostel pillow under your hips.
benefits: Improves blood flow to the pelvic region and ovaries, easing menstrual discomfort.

name: Legs-Up-The-Wall (Viparita Karani)
instructions: Lie down on your back and swing your legs up against a clear wall or hostel wardrobe.
Rest your arms out to the sides, palms facing up.
Close your eyes and breathe slowly through your nose.
Let your hips sink into the floor and release all tension.
safetyPrecautions: If your hamstrings feel tight, scoot your hips a few inches away from the wall.
easierModification: Place a soft pillow under your lower back for elevated comfort.
benefits: Activates the parasympathetic nervous system, easing tension and lowering cortisol (stress hormone) to support hormonal balance in PCOD.

name: Gentle Glute Bridges
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Place your arms at your sides with palms flat.
Press through your heels to lift your hips until your thighs and torso form a straight line.
Pause for 2 seconds at the top, squeezing glutes gently, then slowly lower down.
safetyPrecautions: Do not arch your lower back excessively at the top.
easierModification: Lift hips only halfway up or reduce to 6-8 reps.
benefits: Strengthens posterior chain without stressing joints; large muscle activation improves insulin sensitivity.

name: Wall Push-Ups
instructions: Stand facing a wall, about an arm's length away.
Place your palms flat on the wall at shoulder height and shoulder-width apart.
Slowly bend your elbows and bring your chest toward the wall, keeping your body in a straight plank.
Push through your palms back to the starting position.
safetyPrecautions: Ensure your feet are on a non-slip floor.
easierModification: Step closer to the wall to decrease the angle and effort.
benefits: Builds upper-body strength safely without putting pressure on wrists or knees on the floor.

name: Chair Sit-to-Stands (Box Squats)
instructions: Stand in front of a sturdy chair or hostel bed with feet shoulder-width apart.
Extend your arms forward for balance.
Push your hips back and bend your knees as if sitting down until you lightly touch the chair.
Drive through your heels to return to standing tall.
safetyPrecautions: Keep your knees in line with your toes; do not let knees cave inward.
easierModification: Fully sit on the chair for 1 second between reps before standing up.
benefits: Functional lower body strength that stimulates glucose uptake by the quadriceps.

name: Bird-Dog Core Stabilizer
instructions: Start on hands and knees with a flat back.
Slowly reach your right arm straight forward while extending your left leg straight back.
Hold for 2 seconds while maintaining a level pelvis.
Return to all fours with control, then repeat on opposite sides.
safetyPrecautions: Avoid twisting or dropping your hips to one side.
easierModification: Lift only one leg or one arm at a time without moving both simultaneously.
benefits: Safely strengthens core and spinal stability with zero crunching or abdominal pressure.

name: Post-Meal Brisk Walk (15-20 min)
nameHi: भोजन के बाद 15-20 मिनट की सैर
instructions: Step outside on the campus track, hostel corridors, or nearby garden 20-30 minutes after lunch or dinner.
Maintain a comfortable pace where you can comfortably carry on a conversation.
Swing arms naturally and keep your shoulders relaxed.
safetyPrecautions: Wear supportive walking shoes and stay hydrated in hot weather.
easierModification: Break into two 10-minute sessions or walk in place indoors.
benefits: Supports healthy post-meal glucose management, which is a key gentle lifestyle habit for metabolic wellness in PCOD.

name: Child's Pose (Balasana)
instructions: Kneel on the floor, bring big toes together, and separate knees hip-distance or wider.
Lower your hips toward your heels and fold forward, resting your forehead on the floor or a pillow.
Extend your arms forward or rest them alongside your legs.
Inhale into your lower back and exhale deeply.
safetyPrecautions: If you have knee discomfort, place a rolled towel behind your knees.
easierModification: Place a thick pillow under your chest and abdomen.
benefits: Calms the sympathetic nervous system and decompresses the lumbar spine.

name: Mindful Rest & Hydration Recovery
instructions: Today is dedicated to physical restoration.
Focus on adequate water intake, gentle stretching if desired, and restorative sleep.
Listen to your body without feeling guilty about resting.
safetyPrecautions: Rest is an essential physiological part of fitness and hormonal health, not laziness.
easierModification: A short 5-minute slow stroll if you feel restless.
benefits: Allows muscle fibers to repair and prevents chronic cortisol accumulation.
